**OPERATIONS EXCELLENCE PROGRAM: THE CERTIFIED-SPEED TRANSFORMATION**  
*A Cross-Functional Plan to Cut Industrial-Equipment Lead Time Without Compromising Certified Quality*  

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & THE BURNING PLATFORM

You are losing **one in three competitive deals to delivery speed alone**. Your quoted lead time is **14 weeks**; your fastest rival quotes **six**. Your actual manufacturing and inspection touch-time is almost certainly **well under three weeks**, which means the remaining 11 weeks are queue, waiting, rework loops, inter-departmental friction, and protective padding frozen into the quote because sales does not trust production, and production does not trust quality.

The prior attempt to compress the schedule ended in a **warranty spike that took two years to live down**. That trauma now paralyzes every function:
- **Sales** blames production for sandbagging and quality for bureaucratic gates.
- **Production** blames sales for late/unfrozen specs and quality for unpredictable inspection queues.
- **Quality** blames production for rushed setup and sales for promising dates that force shortcuts.

**The breakthrough insight:** The 14-week schedule is not consumed by *quality work*; it is consumed by *waiting around quality work*. This plan does not eliminate certified inspection gates. It eliminates the **non-value-added time adjacent to them**—and then institutionalizes the cross-functional trust required to prevent a repeat of the warranty crisis.

**Phase 1 Target:** Quote **8–9 weeks** within 9 months.  
**Phase 2 Target:** Quote **6 weeks** within 18 months.  
**Quality Guardrail:** Warranty PPM and first-pass yield (FPY) at each certified gate must **meet or improve** against current baseline; if they degrade, the program pauses before a single further day is compressed.

---

## 2. DIAGNOSTIC: WHERE THE 14 WEEKS ACTUALLY GO

Before changing anything, run a **Value Stream Map (VSM)** on your top two product families. Based on typical industrial-equipment profiles with multi-stage certified inspections, the breakdown will look roughly like this:

| Time Category | Est. Current Duration | What It Really Is | Improvement Category |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sales/Engineering & Spec Freeze** | 1.0 – 2.0 weeks | Order entry errors, ambiguous options, late customer change requests, manual BOM assembly | *Information waste* |
| **Pre-Production Scheduling & Kit Release** | 1.0 – 1.5 weeks | Production-control meetings fighting over priority; missing material calls; batching to “save setup” | *Scheduling waste* |
| **Touch-Time: Fabrication/Machining/Build** | 1.5 – 2.5 weeks | Actual value-added cutting, welding, assembly | **Sacred ground— optimize with SMED, not elimination** |
| **Queue Before Internal Inspection** | 1.5 – 2.5 weeks | Units sitting until QC bay or CMM is free; inspectors waiting for paperwork | *Process waste* |
| **Internal Inspection & Rework Loops** | 1.0 – 2.0 weeks | Some value-added (detection), mostly delay (re-setup, re-inspection) | *Control waste* |
| **Queue Before Certified / Witness Hold-Point** | 2.0 – 3.0 weeks | Waiting for third-party/auditor availability; staging in buffer yard; incomplete pre-certification packages | *External coordination waste* |
| **Certified Inspection (Actual)** | 0.5 – 1.0 week | Actual witness testing, sign-off, documentation | **Protected gate— compress surrounding logistics, not the test itself** |
| **Final Assembly, Paint, Config, Pack** | 1.0 – 1.5 weeks | Waiting for trim parts; batching for paint | *Process waste* |
| **Shipping Prep & Logistics** | 0.5 – 1.0 week | Crating delays; customs doc wait; carrier scheduling | *Logistics waste* |
| **Management Padding / System Slack** | 1.0 – 2.0 weeks | Buffer built into the quote because nobody trusts the system | *Systemic mistrust* |

**Likely finding:** Value-added time ≈ **2–3 weeks**; non-value-added time ≈ **11–12 weeks**.  
The competitor quoting six weeks is not cheating physics; they have simply **removed the waiting**.

---

## 3. THE FOUR LEVERS OF COMPRESSION

### 3.1 Process Re-Engineering: From Serial Gates to Parallel Flow & In-Process Control

**Do not remove certified hold-points. Remove the queues in front of them.**

| Current State (Wrong) | Future State (Right) | Quality Protection |
|---|---|---|
| Build entire unit → send to QC bay → wait → inspect → release | Build to **pre-certified modular stages**; inline SPC/ probing at each stage; module is “certification-ready” before final aggregation | SPC limits and poka-yoke are statistically correlated to the certified test; internal Red-X study proves Module X performance predicts Final Test Y |
| One final functional test at end | **Shadow certification**: run the exact certified protocol internally 48 hours before the witness arrives; official event becomes a confirmatory pass-through | Pre-test uses identical calibrated instruments and procedure; any failure triggers root-cause fix, not waiver |
| 100% final inspection on all specs | **Segmented inspection**: 100% on customer-configuration variables; sampling (AQL plan) on stable base-machine specs with digital traceability | Sampling plan filed with certifying body; digital lot record retention exceeds regulatory minimum |
| Work moves department-to-department in functional batches | **Product-family cells** where a unit flows from raw certified-blank to finished base without leaving the cell | Cell includes an embedded Quality Technician with release authority; inspection is not a department, it is a station with cycle-time parity |

**Specific action:** Move the longest certified inspection (e.g., pressure, electrical safety, or dimensional witness) from the **end** of the line to a **pre-assembly module stage** wherever the standard permits. Final assembly then becomes joining pre-certified halves, reducing the witness-exposure time from days to hours.

### 3.2 Inventory & Configuration Strategy: Decouple the Longest Poles

Industrial equipment is often quoted as engineered-to-order (ETO) when it is actually **configured-to-order (CTO)**.

- **Strategic Pre-Positioning (MTS + ATO):**  
  Build the longest-lead, most stable base sub-assemblies (frames, power modules, common weldments) **to certified stock**. Hold them at a “pre-certified” stage. When an order arrives, finish-machine, configure, paint, and pack. This converts 14-week ETO into 2–4 week final configure-and-certify.
- **Postponement:**  
  Final test and customer-specific options (software, trim, voltage) happen at the end. The certified core is already proven.
- **Buffer Placement (Theory of Constraints):**  
  Place protective **time buffers only in front of the constraint** (the certified witness or the longest-lead machining center). Do not pad every step. This protects the constraint without inflating the total quote.

### 3.3 Scheduling & Execution: Finite Capacity, Frozen Specs, Visible Authority

**Root cause of inter-departmental feud:** Sales sells capacity that does not exist; production hides behind phantom quality delays; quality discovers problems too late.

- **Sales-Configuration Lock:**  
  Implement a **CTO configurator** that generates the quote date based on real available capacity and pre-positioned inventory. Once the customer signs, specs are **frozen**. Any change requires a triad (Sales/Production/Quality) impact review that auto-recalculates the promise date. Sales stops over-promising because the system enforces physics.
- **Finite Capacity Scheduling (FCS):**  
  Replace infinite-capacity MRP with FCS that sequences orders around the constraint (certified test capacity and long-lead machining). Production sees exactly what is possible; Sales sees exactly what is sold.
- **Drum-Buffer-Rope Release:**  
  Do not release raw material to the floor until the constraint is ready for it. This prevents WIP from stacking in front of QC bays.

### 3.4 Supplier & Incoming Material: Extend the Certified Boundary Upstream

Long supplier lead times often dominate the schedule.

- **Source-Certified Supplier Program:**  
  For critical castings, forgings, and electronic assemblies, require suppliers to deliver with **PPAP/ISIR-level documentation** and pre-approved process controls. Shift incoming inspection from “inspect every lot” to **skip-lot / dock-to-line** based on supplier scorecards.
- **Supplier-Managed Inventory (VMI):**  
  Hold certified rough-castings or standard hardware at your dock or in regional 3PL under consignment. You draw against it; supplier owns replenishment.
- **Dual-Source Longest Poles:**  
  Identify any single-source item >4 weeks. Qualify a second source and split 60/40. Competition and redundancy collapse quoted procurement time.

---

## 4. PROTECTING THE QUALITY GATES: THE “NO-REPEAT” WARRANTY COVENANT

The previous warranty spike was caused by **schedule compression that removed inspection or forced production to outrun process validation**. These rules ensure that cannot happen again.

### 4.1 Immutable Principles
1. **No certified hold-point may be eliminated** without written regulatory/customer approval and a statistical process-substitution study (e.g., moving from 100% witness to parametric release per ISO/AS standard).
2. **No overtime or line-speed increase is permitted** on certified operations without a concurrent Engineering/Quality review of setup and tooling fatigue factors.
3. **Quality owns the standard; the Triad owns the schedule.** Quality cannot add unplanned inspection without documenting schedule impact; Production/Sales cannot waive planned inspection to recover a day.

### 4.2 Technical Safeguards
| Risk From Prior Crash | Protective Countermeasure |
|---|---|
| Rushed setup causing downstream defect | **Setup Certification**: First-piece buy-off by Quality **before** the run starts, not after the lot is complete. SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) reduces setup time without rushing setup quality. |
| Hidden defect escaping final gate | **Inline Metrology**: Machine-integrated probing, automated CMM, and vision systems feed SPC dashboards in real time. Defects are caught in the minute, not in the queue. |
| Warranty failure from untested edge-case loads | **Shadow Load Bank / Shadow Protocol**: Run the full certified test recipe on 100% of units internally. The official witness then observes only the final sign-off sequence. |
| Auditor/witness unavailability creating queues | **Auditor Scheduling Agreement**: Contract with certifying body for fixed weekly windows (e.g., “Tuesday/Thursday witness slots”). If the unit is not ready, you lose the slot and absorb the delay—this creates organizational urgency without cutting the test. |

### 4.3 The Pause Mechanism
Establish an **Andon-based pause trigger**: If first-pass yield at any certified gate drops below baseline for two consecutive units, all three functions halt new order release to that cell until Red-X root cause is complete. This proves to Quality that speed will never again be used to override stop-the-line authority.

---

## 5. ALIGNING THE THREE FEUDING FUNCTIONS: FROM BLAME TO SHARED OWNERSHIP

Production, Quality, and Sales are not adversaries; they are hostages to a broken system. Replace functional silos with **cross-functional flow ownership**.

### 5.1 Create the Triad Governance Structure
Form a **“Certified Velocity Office” (CVO)** led by a rotating triumvirate: one senior manager from each function. No single function owns the outcome; all share a P&L metric.

**The Unified Metric:**  
**“Certified Flow Contribution”** = (Gross Margin $ per Order) / (Order Cycle Time in Weeks)

- If Sales promises a reckless date and production incurs overtime/air-freight, margin falls and cycle time is misrepresented → **Triad’s metric drops.**
- If Production delays and expedites later, margin falls → **Triad’s metric drops.**
- If Quality adds rogue inspection without process improvement, cycle time rises → **Triad’s metric drops.**

### 5.2 Rules of Engagement (Memorialized Charter)
| Function | Forbidden Behavior | Required Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Sales** | Promising dates outside configurator output; submitting unfrozen specs after order entry | Uses real-time FCS to quote; specs locked at contract; changes require triad re-date |
| **Production** | Blaming quality for delays caused by internal batching or poor setup discipline | Releases to constraint drum only; maintains certified setup sheets; publishes daily cell throughput |
| **Quality** | Adding ad-hoc holds without schedule impact transparency; inspecting quality *into* the product at end of line | Owns SPC/poka-yoke design; pre-validates processes; inspects at source; reports delay in hours, not mystery |

### 5.3 The Obeya (War Room) Mechanism
- **Physical/digital room** with the VSM on the wall, real-time FCS load, open orders, and warranty PPM trend.
- **Daily 10-minute stand-up** attended by Triad reps: What moved yesterday? What is blocked at a certified gate today? What spec freeze risk is arriving tomorrow?
- **Weekly 60-minute review**: Trade-off decisions only. If Sales needs an express order, the triad jointly decides which buffer to consume or whether to decline the order.

### 5.4 Healing the Scar Tissue
Leadership must formally communicate:  
> *“The prior warranty crisis was caused by removing quality controls to save time. This program removes waiting, not controls. Quality is not the obstacle to speed; it is the prerequisite for sustainable speed.”*

Give Quality an explicit **veto-with-date-impact** authority. When Quality sees a process risk, they pull the Andon; Production responds with fix time, not argument. This rebuilds Quality’s trust, which is the only way they will help compress the schedule.

---

## 6. IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP: 18-MONTH SEQUENCE

**Phase 0: Stabilize & Map (Months 1–3)**  
- Run VSM on two highest-volume families; baseline FPY, warranty PPM, and true queue times.
- Install FCS configurator for Sales; freeze spec process.
- Launch Triad Obeya.
- **Gate:** Identify exactly which 6–8 weeks are NVA and agree they are not “quality time.”

**Phase 1: Pilot Flow & Protect the Gate (Months 4–9)**  
- Convert one product family to cellular flow with embedded QC.
- Implement shadow certification and pre-certified sub-assembly stock.
- Audited supplier skip-lot on top 10 part numbers.
- Target: 14 weeks → **9 weeks** on pilot family.
- **Gate:** Warranty PPM must not rise vs. baseline; FPY at certified stages ≥ current.

**Phase 2: Extend Upstream & Postpone (Months 10–15)**  
- Roll cells to all families >20% revenue.
- VMI/qualified-supplier programs for long-lead items.
- Final paint/configure postponement.
- Target: 9 weeks → **7 weeks**.
- **Gate:** Certified witness windows are now scheduled, not chased.

**Phase 3: Systemic Six-Week Competitiveness (Months 16–18)**  
- TOC drum-buffer-rope fully active; protective buffers optimized via simulation.
- Sales quoting 6–7 weeks depending on configuration complexity.
- National rollout of Triad governance.
- **Gate:** Sustained OTIF ≥95% and warranty PPM ≤ baseline.

---

## 7. EXPECTED OUTCOMES & RISK GOVERNANCE

| Metric | Current | Phase 1 | Phase 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quoted Lead Time | 14 weeks | 9 weeks | 6–7 weeks |
| Estimated NVA Time | ~11–12 weeks | ~6–7 weeks | ~3–4 weeks |
| First-Pass Yield (Certified Gates) | Baseline | ≥ Baseline | ≥ Baseline |
| Warranty PPM | Baseline | ≤ Baseline | ≤ Baseline |
| Win Rate (Speed-contested deals) | ~67% | ~78% | ~85%+ |

**Risk Brake:** If FPY drops or warranty PPM spikes in the pilot cell, the timeline stops at that gate. The Triad must produce a root-cause fix before any additional days are compressed. Speed is the goal; **re-certifying market trust is the boundary.**

---

## 8. FIRST 30 DAYS: WHAT TO DO MONDAY MORNING

1. **CEO/COO charter** the Triad and name the rotating leads.
2. **Baseline one value stream:** Pick the family where you lose the most speed-sensitive deals. Start the VSM.
3. **Freeze the quote engine:** Sales stops quoting 14-week custom ETO on configurable products. Use rough-cut capacity to publish an honest internal range (e.g., 10–14 weeks) immediately.
4. **Shadow run:** On the next three orders, run the certified test protocol internally 48 hours before the witness arrives. Measure how many “surprises” you catch. That number is your warranty risk exposure today.
5. **Obeya first meeting:** Production, Quality, and Sales stand together in front of the VSM. Each marks the step they believe “owns” the most delay. The truth is usually the white space *between* them. That is where your 6-week advantage lives.
